design_judgment.intended_result: Both candidates state an explicit intended user result, a reader decision, and the material design choice, and the bodies deliver them. Source Architecture 02 promises a maintainer can place or split a source unit, decide which imports and exports are legal, distinguish Runtime product code from repository support planes, and judge implementation eligibility 'without reading a manually maintained file inventory'; sections 2 through 10 deliver that through five registered machine contracts, a three-class labeled dependency graph, a five-plane classification, an identity-compared debt set, and an eleven-item conformance floor. Registry 01 promises a maintainer can determine what Runtime versions, which source change creates a new release, how one Skill source exports multiple independently owned Modules, and why authoring layout, provider selection, execution state, and host routing sit outside Registry authority; sections 2 through 9 deliver release identity law, seven owns/does-not-own families, transport-only bundles, provider-independent Module semantic identity, and a seven-decision lifecycle split. Carried note f20 is closed: section 1 now reads 'which release is active for one `RegistryActivationScope` as defined in section 7', so one name is used for the activation key. Carried note f18 is closed on the result surface: `RuntimeCohesionSignalReport` is registered in section 2 and the capsule outputs and 'carries no independent split verdict', which satisfies verification target 9's second half. One residual result defect remains, and it is the reason this revision is not a clean pass: Registry section 11 is a closed-form proof set whose fourteen items never require the atomic admission-unit persistence and sibling-closure independence that section 7 declares as Registry's owned behavior (f21).
design_judgment.authority_structure: Layer, owner, parent, and owned object are valid for both candidates. Each declares layer T2, a canonical_owner equal to its own target path, and parent designDoc/agent_runtime_00_runtime_domain_contract.md; the agent_runtime_ prefix with a non-00 NN mechanically binds both to that unique T1 root under Design Doc Management section 2.3, and both appear in the root candidate's specialization_contracts list. The three owned objects are disjoint: 'Agent Runtime source ownership and dependency architecture', 'immutable Agent Runtime release identity and dependency closure', and the root's 'independently governed Agent Runtime domain'. Verification target 1 is satisfied and reinforced: section 3 rule 6 binds T2 03 and T2 09 implementing source to Execution and declares calls between those units 'intra-Execution dependencies', section 6 exports their public contracts through the Execution namespace, conformance item 4 validates that placement, and the diagram folds both into a labeled Execution node while keeping the supporting foundation and the build-and-conformance tooling plane in separately labeled subgraphs. No seventh responsibility, competing source-owner class, or peer public namespace is created. I tested this fold against Ledger: the root assigns fence-value semantics to 09 but durable fence facts and comparison to 04, so Ledger owns its own fact types and needs no import of 09, and the root graph carries no LEDGER-to-AUTHORITY edge, so the fold introduces no unreachable dependency. Registry's new Policy Enforcement Point claim is substantively correct rather than duplicated authority: Product Authorization section 5 makes every resource-owning service the PEP and section 4 makes publishing a `ResourcePermissionManifest` the resource owner's duty, and Registry states it 'neither issues nor widens permission'. Its peer closure against the root is nevertheless incomplete, because the root still delegates 'Authorization and governed-data ports' to document 09 as one owned specialization with no execution-time scoping (f22, note). The declared peer-owner collisions over canonical filenames 02, 05, and 10 are not claimed closed; I confirmed them independently against designDoc/the_agency_platform.md owned_specialization_contracts (agent_runtime_02_product_target_topology.md and agent_runtime_10_workflow_execution_binding_and_admission_contract.md) and designDoc/the_software_delivery.md owned_specialization_contracts (agent_runtime_05_delivery_roadmap.md). They remain declared adoption blockers and are neither waived nor duplicated as candidate-body findings.
design_judgment.boundary_coherence: The seven dimensions remain distinguishable in both candidates. Source Architecture section 4 assigns ownership 'by the behavior and state transition it implements, not by its current directory, filename, imported technology, or storage location'; section 1 states that logical ownership, source placement, dependency direction, public exposure, and technology binding are separate dimensions that may appear together only when each stays labeled; section 7 classifies five repository planes as planes rather than peers; and section 10 separates the validator's reporting role from repair and from Software Delivery's release decision while denying an AI reviewer any waiver over a deterministic failure. The newly registered `RuntimeCohesionSignalReport` does not mix dimensions with the four declarative manifests: section 2, section 4, and conformance item 11 each label it as derived from `RuntimeSourceOwnershipManifest` and the import graph and deny it an independent verdict, which is the labeled relation Design Doc Management section 6 permits. Registry separates semantic owner (record and schema meaning), authoring authority (Skill Governance plus an external adapter submitting structured bytes), operator surface (the narrow ports of section 8), persistence owner (Data Governance System-of-Record and writer binding), implementation binding (deferred to code-owned schemas), and admission authority (admission, activation, deactivation, withdrawal, host selection, Product Authorization, and Software Delivery release admission held apart by conformance item 7 and the section 11 closing sentence). Carried finding f17's boundary gap is closed exactly as required: section 9 now states 'Data Governance owns migration legality. Software Delivery admits the migration implementation and deployment', restoring the parent's section 9.1 split. One vocabulary boundary is unlabeled: conformance item 9's 'exact scope form' is Product Authorization section 4 manifest vocabulary, not the `RegistryActivationScope` the same document defines six sections earlier, and the candidate does not say which it means (f23, note).

design_judgment.intent_code_separation: Both candidates hold the line. Neither names a current source path, file or line count, provider, model, database product, durable backend, package version, test result, or delivery status. Source Architecture non_goals exclude 'current source-file inventory, line counts, versions, implementation status, or delivery plan'; section 2 pushes exact paths, symbols, exception IDs, hashes, current violations, and generated views to code-owned registrations and refuses 'a prose list, directory scan without registration, or magic file count' as substitutes, which is the correct answer to the code architecture audit's P2.5 magic-count defect; section 8 compares exact debt identities and dispositions rather than an aggregate count, so the baseline cannot be reset to the current tree. Registry non_goals exclude 'current releases, active pointers, provider bindings, database product, or migration status'; section 3 defers exact record fields and any future closed subfamily to code-owned schemas; section 12 defers exact fields and migration to a later Code Design Basis. Carried note f08 remains closed store-neutrally: 'SQL patterns such as `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` are one example of the forbidden behavior, not the store-specific definition of the rule.' Carried findings f03 and f04 remain closed as exact rules: repository plane is a recorded field of `RuntimeSourceOwnershipManifest` and conformance item 10, and item 7 scopes architecture and public-surface projection parity to this contract while assigning Design Contract bundle parity to T2 05, matching root section 13. The remaining illustrative material, namely JSON Schema container keywords in Source Architecture section 5 and transport and capability examples in Registry section 5, is framed as example under Design Doc Management section 3 and does not become the operative rule. Verification target 2 is satisfied across all eight surfaces: repository planes, responsibility ownership, foundation, public namespaces, root exports, migration debt, cohesion signals, and projection parity each have a registered manifest or report plus exactly one conformance item, with no duplicated conformance owner.
design_judgment.implementability: An implementer can form a Code Design Basis for architecture enforcement and for Registry without redesigning either contract or inventing a missing peer. The five machine contracts plus eleven conformance items give the architecture validator a complete input and check set, and they map one-to-one onto the five obligations root section 12 delegates to document 02, namely source ownership, import graph, public namespaces, code cohesion, and migration-debt enforcement, so the declared machine-contract closure a mechanical inheritance check reads is now complete. Registry supplies release families, canonical identity law, closure validation order, the transport-only bundle, the activation key and its uniqueness rule, the lifecycle enforcement boundary with server-side action and resource resolution, a thirteen-row failure table, and a fourteen-item proof set; no invention of authority, product behavior, or a missing peer is required. Verification target 8 is satisfied: the manifest binds all three predecessor reviews by sha256, binds Design Doc Management, Timestamp Semantics, Product Authorization, Data Governance, Skill Governance, Software Delivery, and Contract Audit by sha256, and binds the revision-7 root manifest, which itself binds the candidate Charter, Runtime T0, and T1 root by sha256 with canonical_target mapping; every one of the twenty carried findings appears with identity, source review, severity, affected candidate, correction target, disposition, and correction sections. I independently re-verified each claimed disposition against the candidate text: f01 through f08 remain closed, f09 through f15 remain closed, and f16 through f20 are closed as claimed at the cited sections, and no disposition is false. The single implementability-adjacent residue is not a redesign risk but an unenforceable declared result: section 11's closed form, which revision 4 reaffirmed by closing f16 with a new item rather than by converting the list to a floor, omits section 7's atomic admission-unit persistence and bundle-member independence (f21).

findings.quoted_evidence: Section 7 step 7: "atomically persist each dependency-closed admission unit and its admission result, reusing byte-identical shared dependencies; and". Section 7 closing paragraph: "One candidate failure rejects the affected release closure and every Workflow candidate that depends on it, and identifies the exact defect. It does not block an independent sibling closure merely because both arrived in one transport bundle, does not partially activate anything, and does not repair authoring bytes." Section 11 opens "Registry conformance proves:" and enumerates fourteen items, of which the persistence-bearing items are "13. every persisted Registry class has its required Timestamp and Data Asset registrations, plus separately registered forward and rollback transitions when persistent-schema authority changes; and 14. real persistent-store tests prove schema-release, writer fencing, consumer switch, reconciliation, rollback-window, and migration behavior." Section 10 rows stop at "Non-canonical or hash-mismatched payload | Reject before persistence" and "Missing, mutable, cyclic, or incompatible dependency | Reject the candidate closure".
findings.requirement: Design Doc Management section 6 requires a "declared machine-contract and enforcement handoff" during design audit, and section 6.1 requires that the design guide implementation without forcing the reviewer to infer missing authority. The revision-7 Charter section 7 condition 1 requires that an external domain plugin can register dependency-closed immutable releases through public interfaces alone, and section 7 requires that unmet conditions be reported as real gaps rather than covered by a passing surface. The revision-7 T1 root section 2 assigns Registry "Immutable release closure, admission, activation, deactivation, withdrawal, exact retrieval, and Registry-store schema lifecycle", and section 13 consumes Registry's conformance evidence for the "Canonical Registry and Ledger authority" evidence family, adding that "Missing evidence leaves the corresponding Charter condition unsatisfied." Contract Audit section 6 makes the aggregate verdict depend on the declared layer's completion, and section 5 states that "A reviewer cannot waive a failed deterministic invariant", which presupposes that the required invariant is declared.
findings.impact: Section 11 is a closed-form proof set. Revision 4 confirmed that reading by closing predecessor finding f16 with a new item 9 rather than by converting the opening to "proves at least", the phrasing the sibling Source Architecture candidate uses in its section 9 ("Architecture conformance validates at least:"). Under the closed reading, none of the fourteen items requires that one dependency-closed admission unit and its admission result commit atomically, and none requires that an independent sibling closure in the same transport bundle still be admitted when another member fails. Item 4 proves only that one Skill source exports Modules "without shared lifecycle or sibling re-versioning", which is a versioning and Skill-source property, not admission-failure isolation across a bundle that may carry schemas, prompts, policies, profiles, adapters, and Workflows from several sources. Two required results are therefore unenforceable. A Registry that satisfies all fourteen items can commit a release record without its resolved closure after a crash or concurrent writer, breaking section 1's owned result of "individually identified immutable releases and one exact dependency closure" and Charter condition 1; and it can reject an entire bundle on one member's failure, reinstating exactly the bundle-level lifecycle coupling that section 4's transport-only bundle exists to prevent and that the review brief lists as a headline material decision and reviewer question 4. Section 10 carries no failure row for either result either, so neither the proof set nor the failure table names the behavior. This is a completion gate that can pass while the required system result is absent.

It publishes a `ResourcePermissionManifest` for activation, deactivation, and withdrawal. ... It neither issues nor widens permission and declares no dependency on the T2 09 External Authority Integration ports." Revision-7 root section 2: "| `agent_runtime_09_external_authority_integration_contract.md` | Authorization and governed-data ports, operation intents, decision observations, fence-value semantics, invalidation, late-result quarantine, and newly authorized compensation requests | Durable fence facts and comparison owned by document 04; finalization timing, Workflow advancement, event lifecycle, and Runtime state transitions owned by document 10 |". findings.requirement: Design Doc Management section 4 required order item 2 states that when a proposal "creates, promotes, splits, merges, replaces, or renames a registered structure, compare the complete same-level peer set and record every keep, merge, move, replace, or retire disposition in the candidate or its rewrite plan." Section 2.3 states that a T2 "cannot create a second domain root or widen its parent's semantic authority." Product Authorization section 5 requires that "The resource-owning service or Gateway is the Policy Enforcement Point", and section 4 requires that "Each resource-owning service publishes a code-owned `ResourcePermissionManifest` containing its resource types, atomic actions, scope forms, condition schema, and grant requirement class."
findings.impact: Registry's Policy Enforcement Point claim is substantively correct and is required rather than invented: Product Authorization sections 4 and 5 impose it on every resource-owning service, and it is structurally forced here, because Source Architecture section 3 rule 6 places the T2 09 ports inside Execution source while EXECUTION-to-REGISTRY is an allowed edge, making REGISTRY-to-EXECUTION a forbidden reverse edge. Registry could not consume 09's ports even if it wanted to. The defect is that the root still delegates "Authorization and governed-data ports" to document 09 as one owned specialization, and lists one external-authorization port family in its section 12 machine contracts, without stating that authorization-port ownership is scoped to execution-time protected operations or that each Runtime responsibility owning protected resources is the enforcement point for those resources. The root body is consistently execution-scoped for document 09 in sections 6, 7, 8, and 10, so a careful reader resolves the ambiguity, but the section 2 delegation table is the surface a future T2 09 author reads, and Design Doc Management section 6 treats ambiguous prose as a design finding when it changes who may decide or write. Registry cannot narrow a sibling's delegated ownership from its own contract without widening its own authority, so the correction cannot safely be applied inside the candidate. Left unstated, the next slice can produce two Runtime-owned authorization seams whose overlap surfaces only in implementation. This does not block a Code Design Basis for Registry, whose own seam is fully specified.

Do not relocate this correction into the Registry candidate. Once the root states the boundary, Registry may cite it in section 8 instead of only disclaiming a dependency on the T2 09 ports.

findings.quoted_evidence: Section 11 item 9: "the published lifecycle `ResourcePermissionManifest` covers activation, deactivation, and withdrawal with exact scope form and grant requirement class, and rejects an action or release resource absent from that manifest". Section 7: "A `RegistryActivationScope` is exactly one `(release_family, stable_object_id)` logical object. It contains no tenant, host, product route, environment, Cell, region, deployment, or provider identity. Activation selects at most one current admitted version in that scope. ... Withdrawal makes an admitted release ineligible for new selection while preserving historical execution validity."
findings.requirement: Product Authorization section 4 defines "scope forms" as one field of a resource-owning service's manifest, alongside "resource types, atomic actions, ... condition schema, and grant requirement class". Design Doc Management section 6 states that "Ambiguous prose is not merely a writing defect when it changes who can decide, write, review, or admit", and predecessor finding f20 required this candidate to "use one name for the activation key it now defines".
findings.impact: Revision 4 closed f20 by making `RegistryActivationScope` the single name for the activation key, then introduced a second, unrelated use of "scope" in the same document's conformance list. Item 9's "exact scope form" is Product Authorization manifest vocabulary describing which resource instances a permission covers; `RegistryActivationScope` is the activation-selection key. They are not the same object, and conflating them produces a wrong manifest: withdrawal in section 7 applies to one admitted release version, which no `(release_family, stable_object_id)` pair identifies, so withdrawal entries specified against the activation scope could not name their resource. A related smaller drift sits in the same sentence: the grammatical subject of "rejects an action or release resource absent from that manifest" is the manifest, whereas section 8 and the section 10 failure row correctly assign the refusal to the Registry writer. Neither point blocks a Code Design Basis, because Product Authorization section 4 supplies the correct reading, but the candidate does not label which vocabulary item 9 uses.

No Source Architecture change is required for adoption of this slice. All twenty carried findings are independently verified closed at the sections the manifest claims, and no claimed disposition is false: T2 03 and T2 09 source and public contracts belong to Execution with no seventh responsibility or peer namespace; repository planes, responsibility ownership, foundation, public namespaces, root exports, migration debt, cohesion signals, and projection parity each have exactly one registered artifact and one conformance item with no duplicated authority; foundation instant validation is bounded by Timestamp Semantics and denied any protected predicate; RegistryActivationScope is exactly (release_family, stable_object_id) with the required exclusions, a per-scope uniqueness item, and an active-selection-conflict refusal; the Registry writer is the Policy Enforcement Point with a registered lifecycle ResourcePermissionManifest covering activation, deactivation, and withdrawal and refusing absent actions or resources; persistent-schema changes bind separately registered Data Governance forward and rollback transitions with writer fencing, consumer switch, reconciliation, and an explicit rollback window, with Data Governance owning migration legality and Software Delivery admitting implementation and deployment; Registry declares Product Authorization, Data Governance, Timestamp Semantics, and Software Delivery; the manifest binds all three predecessor reviews and every inherited authority by sha256 and carries every finding identity, severity, affected candidate, correction target, disposition, and correction location; and the Inspection-to-foundation edge is present so diagram and policy agree while the registered cohesion signal report remains a non-verdict projection.
